main_text.p: Iustinus, & Diodorus Siculus, & Plinius affirmant. Et hic quidem quotannis Herculi suo sacra hujusmodi Poenos fecisse libro xxx. cap. v. scribit. Iustinus verò ex Trogo etiam recitat, Darium Hystaspis fil. Persarum regem per legatos, quos ad petenda in Græcos auxilia Carthaginem miserat, cum civitate egisse, ut hoc genere sacrificii inposterum abstineret, idque civitatem tunc promisisse. Promisso tamen non stetisse, verba Platonis & Diodori ac Plinii satis arguunt. Aliam legem abfurdam eorundem recenset Iustinus, occasione sceleris à cive commissi latam. Nam cum Hanno imperator bellum contra Dionysium seniorem in Sicilia prioribus annis peste exercitum depopulante desertum, volente civitate majoribus viribus instauraret, Suniator quidam civis præpotens, inimicus Hannonis, ut huic malefaceret, apparatum omnem cum obtrectatione imperatoris per literas Græco sermone conscriptas Dionysio enunciasse perhibetur. Sed literis interceptis autor comprehensus, & prodītionis damnatus. Tum ex senatusconsulto lata lex, ne quis in posterum Carthaginiensis Græcas literas, aut sermonem Græcum disceret, ne aut loqui cum hoste, aut scribere ad
main_text.notes: Show-through and edge marks at the left margin and the faint mirrored characters at the bottom right are not printed text of this page and are left out. No catchword or signature is clearly legible. The paragraph division is uncertain: the lines show no clear indents, so the page is set as one running paragraph continuing from the previous page. "Suniator" and "prodītionis" were read as printed; "prodītionis" may be a printing variant of "prodītionis" and the final macron is doubtful [?]. Long s has been normalised to s throughout.
